title: Input & Events 🔘
description: Handle button clicks, text input, and create interactive HUDs.

slides.title: Widget Events 📡
slides.content:
# Interactivity

Widgets can fire events:

* **OnClicked** (Button) – when clicked.
* **OnPressed / OnReleased** (Button) – mouse down / up.
* **OnHovered / OnUnhovered** (Button) – mouse enter / exit.
* **OnTextChanged / OnTextCommitted** (Editable Text Box) – text input.

These appear in the Details panel under **Events**. Click the **+** to create a node in the Graph.

quizData.question: Which event fires when a button is clicked?
quizData.explanation: OnClicked fires when the button is pressed and released over the same area.

slides.title: Button Click Example 🖱️
slides.content:
## Print on Click

1. Add a **Button** to your widget, with a **Text** child saying "Click Me".
2. In the Details panel for the Button, find Events → **OnClicked** → click the **+**.
3. The Graph opens with an **OnClicked** node. Drag off → add **Print String**.
4. Compile, add the widget to viewport, Play, and click the button. The message appears!

You can also access other widgets from the Graph using the **Get Widget** node or by binding a variable.

slides.title: Editable Text Box ⌨️
slides.content:
## Player Input

An **Editable Text Box** lets players type.

* **Text** – the current content.
* **Hint Text** – placeholder when empty.
* **OnTextChanged** – fires every keystroke.
* **OnTextCommitted** – fires when user presses Enter or clicks away.

Use OnTextCommitted to validate or save input. Use OnTextChanged for live search filtering.

quizData.question: OnTextCommitted fires after every character typed.
quizData.explanation: OnTextCommitted fires when the user finishes editing (loses focus or presses Enter). OnTextChanged fires on every change.

slides.title: Focus & Navigation 🎮
slides.content:
## Controller Support

For gamepad/keyboard navigation:

* Use **Set Keyboard Focus** to direct input to a specific widget.
* Enable **Is Focusable** on widgets.
* Use **Navigation** settings in the Details panel to define up/down/left/right targets.

This is crucial for console games. Without it, UI won't respond to controller.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use the Widget Interaction Component

For VR or 3D UIs, add a **Widget Interaction Component** to a pawn. It simulates mouse clicks on 3D widgets.
